badges_over_time.title: Badges over time
badges_over_time.subtitle: Each step is a gym badge, then each Elite Four member and the Champion beaten, at the time it happened. Every model’s best run, against keepingiticy’s English-language world record.
notes: * Heavily assisted: the Rayquaza lane adds help to the harness. The Qwen lane runs follow a just-in-time guide to the next milestone. The Opus lane run has no guide, only four one-time hints and a Mach Bike dash tool. Dotted lines and hollow end points are lane runs.
keepingiticy’s Elite Four splits aren’t marked; the line runs from the Rain Badge to the Champion at 2:28:39. Unassisted Opus ran out of time against Drake.

Unassisted Qwen3.6, Qwen3.8 and GLM start from a main-menu save with fast text already set; every other run, the Rayquaza lane runs included, starts from power-on. Unassisted Opus is one chain of four linked legs, stitched at the checkpoints each leg loaded.

badges_for_the_money.title: Badges for the money
badges_for_the_money.subtitle: Each model’s best run: how far it got (gym badges, then the Elite Four and Champion) against what the tokens would have cost at API prices, up to that point.
notes: * Heavily assisted (Rayquaza lane), shown as hollow points. Unassisted Opus’s cost is up to Glacia, the third of the Elite Four.

Prices: frontier models at their API list prices (Opus from its gateway session records; Astra and Sol from Codex token counts; DeepSeek from recorded tokens at OrcaRouter’s list price). Local models (estimated) are priced at the cheapest OpenRouter provider for each model’s recorded tokens, as of 11/11.
